name: decomposition-synthesis
title: Decomposition synthesis — the cross-arm landscape
question: Across all seven decomposition strategies, what is the speed x accuracy x composability landscape, and which strategy wins for which regime?
hypothesis: No single arm dominates: the monolith is fastest+most accurate but least composable; native/biological seams trade speed for composability; the choice is regime-dependent and the tradeoff map makes the frontier explicit.
objective: Aggregate every arm's runtime, accuracy, overhead and composability into one cross-arm comparison and a decision guide.
description: The synthesis node of the SBML-decomposition investigation. It builds-on all seven arm studies, carrying each arm's results forward as inputs (RFC-0006 provides/outputs_used), and renders the investigation-wide comparison: the composability scorecard, the runtime + overhead breakdowns, the accuracy divergence, the speed-accuracy-composability tradeoff map, and the decision table. These are investigation-scope views (every one spans 4-6 arms) and live here rather than under any single arm, where they would read as being about that one arm.
claim: The seven arms span a speed-accuracy-composability frontier with no dominant point; the tradeoff map + decision table turn that frontier into a regime-specific recommendation.
